system.description:
BAIT

Bait is found only via camp activities or specific merchants.

Merchants who sell bait are rare, limited only to spots where fishing should be common and expected. It is up to the GM to discern if a bait-selling merchant is appropriate for the location.

Bait is designed to be limited, with a recommendation for each player only being able to buy up to 10 units of bait per session. An example Zenit conversion is at least 20 Zenit for 1 simple bait.

CAMP ACTIVITIES

With the addition of the Angler class comes a special Camp Activity available for resting scenes.

CAMP ACTIVITY

TARGET

You spend your time looking for bait in the area; describe how and roll 1d6. (@UUID[Compendium.fabula-ultima-homebrew.homebrew-rollable-tables.RollTable.EdwaC4A1eZVFUYNW]{Bait Finding})

  • 1. None, really? You do not manage to find bait, and you wear yourself out so that you do not recover Hit Points and Mind Points during this rest.

  • 2. It's Something, I guess... You find 1 Simple Bait.

  • 3-5. A respectable find! You find 3 Simple Bait.

  • 6. No way! You find 1 Unique Bait.

FISHING

Fishing works by making use of a fishing dice: it determine if you would be able to catch a fish in that particular area. The GM determines the fishing die based on how feasible it would be to catch a fish in that spot.

OPTIONAL RULE: BAD TIMES

There can be times where fishing leads to minor or major disasters. This is where the Bad Times optional rule comes to play.

On rolling the max value on a fishing die starting on a d12, the GM may opt to choose a Danger that appropriately fits the scenario. Characters should generally be able to overcome a danger through a series of Checks or a Conflict scene.

  • The risk of losing an important item.

  • A dangerous fish inflicting Status Effects.

  • A fish has decided to fight back.

  • A tiny fish hell bent on ruining your day.

  • Trash and litter that you would need to sort.

It is unlikely for the characters to be directly damaged by Bad Times, but in the case where this happens, refer to the damage table provided in the Dangers section of the Core Rulebook (page 108).

WEAPONRY FISH

Fish can be used by the Angler as deadly weapons for combat.

Note that an Angler can still use these fish even if they normally lack the ability to handle martial weapons, and all weaponry fish are one-handed unless stated otherwise. The damage type of the fish then depends on the origin of the fish (see Origin to Damage Type Conversion table).

ITEM FISH / ZENIT REWARD

There are instances where the fish caught by the Angler is not fit for combat, but works well as components for other things such as delicacies and projects. These fish would have qualities based on their origins designed by the GM.

Check the Winter Holiday Bonus 2022: Forging Rules to see example of potential qualities based on origin.

DISCOVERY FISH

During the course of your fishing journey, there are chances for the character to reel in special fishes called Discovery Fish.

Discovery Fishes are by design an uncommon occurrence, so the GM should make sure each and every one of them is useful (as well as interesting!). Feel free to make Discovery Fish better between bait tiers: a Discovery found without using bait should not be as good as Discovery found with Unique-rank bait.

DISCOVERY FISH EXAMPLES

NO BAIT

Bomb Fish

Deal minor damage to all enemies.

Healing Fish

Heals an ally for 30 Hit Points.

Status Fish

Cure an ally of one Status effect.

SIMPLE BAIT

Domination Fish

Choose a target. For their next turn, they have to choose their ally as their target for attacks and spells.

Shield Fish

Choose a target. Until the start of your next turn, your ally is covered under guard rules and cannot be targeted.

Type Fish

Until the start of your next turn, all of your ally attacks become a specific type.


UNIQUE BAIT

Fish Fish

Choose a soldier or elite-rank target. Until the end of your next turn, the target is turned into a Thornfish and is limited to work with that stat block.

Piercing Fish

Until the start of your next turn, all of your ally attacks gain multi(2).

Shipping Fish

Choose a target. Until the start of your next turn, they are compelled to focus their attention on you.


Note that Discovery Fish are different from both Weaponry and Item Fish (they are not to be created as weapons or ingredients/crafting components) and are still designed to be consumable (they are destroyed upon use). Similar to all fish, they require an Action to use.
